package_info.why_malicious: The package 'discord-hacker' contains code that exfiltrates sensitive Discord authentication tokens from the environment and sends them to an external attacker-controlled server during package installation, enabling credential theft and potential account compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value via HTTPS POST to malicious.example.com/api/steal, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Reads the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obtains sensitive Discord authentication token from the environment.

attack_chain.action: Sends the stolen token to an external attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltrates credentials to the attacker, enabling account compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Access to DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable during npm package installation.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to malicious.example.com/api/steal from install scripts.
file_indicators: postinstall.js containing code that references process.env.DISCORD_TOKEN
Presence of HTTPS request logic targeting malicious.example.com in install scripts
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to /api/steal endpoint during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installation scripts for access to sensitive environment variables such as DISCORD_TOKEN. Flag any install-time scripts that initiate outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains like malicious.example.com, especially when transmitting environment variable values. Use file scanning to detect references to process.env.DISCORD_TOKEN and hardcoded network destinations in postinstall.js or similar install scripts.
